answer: CERT-In incident reporting six hours noticing

From the sources we checked (KB as of 2026-11-07):
- CERT-In Directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000, Direction (ii) [IN-CERTIN-DIR-2022-ii] (verified record): Annexure I incidents go to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them. The CERT-In FAQ explains severity and scale criteria for applying the deadline.
- CERT-In / SIA-India Cyber Security Framework and Guidelines for Space including Satellite Communication, §3.2.1 [IN-SPACEFW-2026-3-2-1] (verified record): Repeats the six-hour CERT-In clock for satellite operators; §7.1 (PDF p. 33) says the same.
- Up to four reports to three bodies, with two different triggers [GAP-IN-01-REPORTING-CLOCKS] (gap register, human-confirmed): For one NTN incident a telecom entity reports to CERT-In within six hours of noticing it and to DoT within six hours of becoming aware of it (details within 24 hours).
